title: Metabolic profiling of body fluids and multivariate data analysis
author: Trezzi, Jäger, et al.
materials: Metabolite extraction (in triplicate for each sample):1.Mix 10 μL of either plasma, serum, CSF or saliva with 90 μL extraction fluid (−20 °C) in a 1.5-ml-reaction tube for quenching. We recommend to aliquot the extraction fluid before adding the samples and to keep all samples on ice.2.Vortex thoroughly3.Shake for 5 min on Thermomixer at 1400 rpm, 4 °C4.Centrifuge for 5 min at 16,000 × g, 4 °C5.Transfer 70 μL supernatant (contains metabolites) in GC vials with micro insert. Optionally, keep the pellet for protein extraction if applicable (see below)6.Dry supernatant in a refrigerated rotary vacuum evaporator at −4 °C for a minimum of 1 h. Important: Make sure the samples are completely dry7.Before taking out the vials, allow the refrigerated rotary vacuum evaporator to warm up to RT for 30 min to prevent water condensation in vials. This avoids problems during derivatization which is highly sensitive to humidity.8.Tightly cap vials and store at −80 °C until GC–MS measurement

steps.title: Thaw samples at 4 °C
steps.instruction: Place frozen body‑fluid samples on wet ice or in a cooling rack and allow them to thaw at 4 °C, keeping them cold to prevent biochemical reactions; process the thawed samples immediately.

steps.title: Aliquot and quench samples
steps.instruction: Remove three identical aliquots from each sample (technical triplicates) and quench each by adding a methanol‑water mixture to suppress all biochemical activity and precipitate proteins.

steps.title: Prepare extraction fluid with internal standard
steps.instruction: Make an internal‑standard solution by diluting [U13C]Ribitol in Milli‑Q water to 45 µg mL⁻¹; then mix 8 vol MeOH with 1 vol of this solution to obtain the extraction fluid (pre‑chilled at –20 °C) containing 5 µg mL⁻¹ [U13C]Ribitol. Store the fluid at –20 °C until use.

steps.title: Extract metabolites (triplicate)
steps.instruction: For each technical replicate, add 10 µL of plasma, serum, CSF or saliva to 90 µL of the –20 °C extraction fluid in a 1.5 mL reaction tube, keep on ice, vortex, shake 5 min on a Thermomixer at 1400 rpm and 4 °C, centrifuge 5 min at 16 000 × g and 4 °C, transfer 70 µL supernatant to GC vials with micro‑insert, dry the supernatant in a refrigerated rotary vacuum evaporator at –4 °C for ≥1 h, warm the evaporator to room temperature for 30 min before opening, tightly cap vials and store at –80 °C until GC‑MS.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 µL sample to 90 µL chilled extraction fluid in a 1.5 mL tube.
Keep tubes on ice and vortex thoroughly.
Shake 5 min at 1400 rpm, 4 °C on Thermomixer.
Centrifuge 5 min at 16 000 × g, 4 °C.
Transfer 70 µL supernatant to GC vial with micro‑insert.
Dry supernatant at –4 °C in refrigerated rotary vacuum evaporator for at least 1 h until completely dry.
Allow evaporator to warm to room temperature for 30 min before removing vials.
Cap vials tightly and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Optional: Preserve pellet for proteomics
steps.instruction: After centrifugation, dry the remaining pellet in the refrigerated rotary vacuum evaporator at –4 °C and store at –80 °C for later DNA/RNA/protein analysis.

steps.title: Derivatize samples for GC‑MS
steps.instruction: Perform the two‑step automated derivatization: first react the dried extract with methoxyamine hydrochloride, then silylate with N‑methyl‑N‑trimethylsilyl‑trifluoroacetamide (MSTFA) according to the instrument’s protocol before GC‑MS measurement.

steps.title: Configure GC‑MS method
steps.instruction: Set the GC‑MS instrument (e.g., Agilent 7890A + 5975C) with the following parameters: inlet split/splitless at 270 °C, split ratio 10:1, injection volume 1 µL, helium carrier gas at 1.2 mL min⁻¹ (constant), oven program 90 °C for 1 min then ramp to 320 °C at 15 °C min⁻¹ and hold 8 min (total run 24.3 min), transfer line 280 °C, ion source 230 °C, quadrupole 150 °C, electron ionization 70 eV, scan range m/z 70–700 at ≥4 scans s⁻¹.

substeps.instruction: Set inlet temperature to 270 °C.
Select split ratio 10:1 and injection volume 1 µL.
Use helium as carrier gas at a constant flow of 1.2 mL min⁻¹.
Program oven: 90 °C for 1 min, ramp to 320 °C at 15 °C min⁻¹, hold 8 min (total 24.3 min).
Set transfer line to 280 °C and ion source to 230 °C.
Set quadrupole temperature to 150 °C.
Use electron ionization at 70 eV and acquire full‑scan spectra from m/z 70 to 700 with a minimum scan rate of 4 scans s⁻¹.

steps.title: Run GC‑MS analysis
steps.instruction: Inject each derivatized sample (1 µL) into the configured GC‑MS system and acquire data according to the method described above.

steps.title: Deconvolute raw GC‑MS data
steps.instruction: Process the acquired files with MetaboliteDetector (v2.5 or higher) using the following deconvolution settings: peak threshold 5, minimum peak height 5, bins per scan 10, deconvolution width 5 scans, no baseline adjustment, minimum 15 peaks per spectrum, no minimum base‑peak intensity requirement.

steps.title: Calibrate retention index
steps.instruction: Perform retention‑index calibration using a C10–C40 even n‑alkane mixture according to the software’s instructions.

steps.title: Normalize metabolite intensities
steps.instruction: For each metabolite, calculate the average intensity of the two nearest QC pool samples (chronologically) and divide the sample’s intensity by this average.

substeps.instruction: Identify the two QC pool (reference) samples that flank the sample in the run order.
Calculate the average intensity of the metabolite across these two pools.
Divide the sample’s metabolite intensity by the calculated average to obtain the normalized value.

steps.title: Assess GC‑MS quality with internal standards
steps.instruction: Monitor internal‑standard signals across the sequence to detect sensitivity drift and to flag samples with abnormal extraction efficiency as outliers.

steps.title: Statistical analysis and classification
steps.instruction: Partition the normalized dataset into training and test sets, fit a logistic‑regression model by maximum‑likelihood estimation on the training set, evaluate performance on the test set using ROC curves to determine an optimal decision threshold, and apply cross‑validation or regularization to guard against over‑fitting.

substeps.instruction: Split the data into training and test subsets.
Fit a logistic‑regression model on the training data using maximum‑likelihood estimation.
Generate ROC curves on the test data and select an optimal decision threshold.
Validate the model with cross‑validation or regularization to avoid over‑fitting.
Predict class probabilities for unknown samples using the final model.
